newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth earnings rise on wireless growth.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth earnings rise on wireless growth.

text.p: BellSouth Corp. said Monday its profits climbed 4 percent in the second quarter, led by robust growth in its wireless services division.

The Atlanta-based Baby Bell operator said net income rose to $654 million, or 66 cents a share, from $629 million or 63 cents a share a year ago. Revenues for the period totalled $4.92 billion, compared with $4.62 billion in the same year-ago quarter.
"We're continuing to achieve excellent current results while making the investments we need to keep earnings growth going in the future," BellSouth President Duane Ackerman said in a statement.

BellSouth's core revenues, for its local telephone service unit, grew just 2 percent to $2.07 billion from $2.02 billion. Sluggish growth there, however, was more than offset by the continuing rapid sales growth in its wireless and auxiliary services units.
Domestic cellular revenues rose 11.5 percent to $625.7 million. International cellular revenues grew 66 percent to $382.9 million.

Much of that increase came from new customers. The domestic wireless division posted customer growth of 21 percent from a year ago, while international wireless operations grew by 83 percent, especially in its core international markets in Argentina, Chile and Venezuela.
Sales of ancillary products and features such as call waiting and MemoryCall voice messaging grew at a rate of 25 percent, the company said.

BellSouth also installed a record number of additional access lines -- 121,000 -- in its residential customers' homes during the period. Thirteen percent of its residential customers have now had additional lines installed.
"Excellent earnings out of BellSouth," Montgomery Securities analyst Bill Vogel said. "We are pretty bullish on the rest of the year. Everything we saw in the quarter looks great."
The strong earnings led BellSouth's chief financial officer to predict the company would have little difficulty meeting Wall Street's earnings expectations for the remainder of the year.
CFO Ronald Dykes told Reuters he expected to match analysts' estimates of $2.80 a share for the year even though doing so "implies double-digit growth for the rest of the year."
"I'm not at all uncomfortable with that," Dykes said.
Dykes said he was particularly optimistic about growth prospects for the company's international cellular division and for the installation of additional access lines in residential customers' homes.
BellSouth rose 69 cents a share to $45.75 in consolidated New York Stock Exchange trading Monday.
